title: In affine chains, persistence and composition across time are decided by two row sequences of M^T
subject: Reducing the contact-network gate across time, on affine chains of three rings, to linear recurring sequences over GF(2)
conclusion: For chains of three rings with linear or affine rules, each ring its own, and affine contact laws chosen at each contact, the value of contact c at lag T is the parity of the first-row cells in r_T(c) = e_c M^T plus a constant, so c binds two rings at T exactly when r_T(c) meets both, and the chain composes at T exactly when r_T(c2) meets both end rings. Each sequence r_T(c) is eventually periodic, so whether both contacts persist and the chain composes at every lag from the light-cone lag on is decided exactly by iterating the two row vectors until they repeat, and for one finite chain that iteration is a complete proof of its verdicts.
